newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via three-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via three-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is seen adding temporary reserves to the banking system on Monday through three-day system repurchase agreements, Fed watchers said.
"We're expecting the Fed to inject reserves with a three-day system RP, probably for fixed collateral," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
Saporta said she sees the Fed's daily average add need at around $5.0 billion during the current two-week liquidity maintenance period.
Analysts at consulting firm MMS International Inc also expect the Fed to add reserves to the system on Monday through three-day system RPs.
Pundits also said the Fed may add permanent reserves to the system this week through a bill pass operation.
"We're expecting a bill pass sometime soon, perhaps as early as this Wednesday. If not, we will be looking for that operation on November 6," Saporta said.
At 1015 EDT/1515 GMT, the Federal funds rate was at 5-5/16 percent, just above the central bank's 5-1/4 percent target.
